subtopics.title: The Job of the CRJ and Its Source Documents

questions.question: The single job of the Cash Receipts Journal is to record:
options: All money received by the business, in date order, for one month
All money paid and received in one book
Only cash sales, nothing else
The balances of all ledger accounts

questions.question: Which source document proves a day's cash sales in the CRJ?
options: The duplicate deposit slip
The cash register roll, totalled at close of business
A supplier's invoice
The bank statement only

questions.question: The difference between the analysis column and the Bank column is that:
options: Analysis records payments; Bank records receipts
Analysis is only used for capital deposits
The two columns always carry different totals
Analysis captures each amount as it is received; Bank records the total actually deposited

subtopics.title: Recording Cash Sales — Two Truths per Sale

questions.question: Lindi's General Store marks goods up 50 percent on cost. Goods sell for R1 800 cash. Cost of sales is:
options: R900 — half of the selling price
R1 200 — selling price divided by 1,5

questions.question: Why is the cost of sales figure entered in the CRJ even though no cash moved for it?
options: It records the stock leaving at cost, keeping Trading Stock truthful
It doubles the day's income
The bank requires two figures per deposit
It replaces the need for a register roll

questions.question: One cash-sale line in the CRJ feeds which four accounts at month end?
options: Bank, Capital, Rent Income, Drawings
Bank, Sales, Cost of Sales, Trading Stock
Sales, Purchases, Creditors, Bank
Trading Stock, Capital, Bank, Wages

questions.question: The check that the cost figure is correct is:
options: R1 200 minus 50 percent gives R600
R1 800 times 1,5 gives R2 700
R1 800 minus R900 gives R900
R1 200 times 1,5 returns the R1 800 selling price

questions.question: The owner deposits R60 000 additional capital. In the CRJ this amount appears in:
options: The Sales column, because money came in
The Cost of Sales column
Analysis, Bank, and the Sundry accounts column with the detail 'Capital'
The Bank column only, with no further detail

questions.question: Sales gets a dedicated column while Rent income does not because:
options: Rent is not really income
Cash sales happen daily, so one column total can be posted for the whole month; rent arrives rarely
Rent income is recorded in the Cash Payments Journal
The sundry column is reserved for expenses

questions.question: Which receipt does NOT belong in this term's Grade 10 CRJ?
options: Money received from debtors — that column is added when credit transactions begin
A tenant paying rent
The owner depositing capital
A day's cash sales

questions.question: For the month, Sales totalled R4 500 and Sundries R63 200. The cross-cast requires the Bank column total to be:
The Cost of Sales total stands outside the cross-cast because:
options: It is not money received — it is the parallel stock record
It is always equal to the Sales total
It has already been posted to the ledger
It belongs to next month's journal

questions.question: At month end the Cost of Sales total is posted as:
options: Debit Trading Stock, credit Bank
Debit Cost of Sales, credit Trading Stock
Debit Sales, credit Cost of Sales
Debit Bank, credit Cost of Sales

questions.question: In the diary picture, the CRJ is simply:
options: A list of everything the business owes
A money-in diary: date, proof, source, amount — one line per receipt
A summary of the bank statement
The owner's personal spending record

questions.question: Sales earns its own column in the diary because:
options: It is the regular — writing it a column makes the month quick to add
The word is short to write
Sales amounts are always the same
The owner prefers it

questions.question: The R60 000 the owner moved into the business is treated as:
options: A regular with its own lane
An amount left out of the diary
A named visitor — written in the open sundry column with its name
A sale at zero cost

subtopics.title: The Double Line — What the Customer Pays and What the Shelf Loses

questions.question: Goods sold for R1 800 at a 50 percent mark-up on cost. The shelf's number — the cost — is found by:
options: Dividing R1 800 by 1,5 to get R1 200
Taking 50 percent off R1 800 to get R900
Adding 50 percent to R1 800
Halving R1 800 and adding R100

questions.question: The pair of numbers R1 800 in and R1 200 off the shelf tells Lindi immediately that:
options: She owes the supplier R600
The till is short by R600
Her rent is covered for the day
She made R600 gross profit today — the perpetual system at work

questions.question: The analysis column works like:
options: A counting-tray — collecting each amount as it arrives until the total is banked
A price list for the shelf
A record of goods returned
The ledger's debit side

questions.question: The month-end handshake test is:
options: Sales total plus Cost of Sales total equals Sundries
Sales total plus Sundries total must equal the Bank column total
Bank total minus Sundries equals Cost of Sales
Analysis total must equal Cost of Sales total

questions.question: The lanes add to R67 700 but the Bank column shows R68 100. The bookkeeper should:
options: Post the totals anyway and fix it later
Change the Bank total to R67 700
Hunt the R400 difference — an amount reached Bank unexplained, or a lane amount missed Bank
Add R400 to the Sales column

questions.question: The Cost of Sales column never joins the handshake because:
options: It is the shelf's record, not money received
Its total is always too large
It is only totalled at year end
It belongs to the Cash Payments Journal
